name: TRAVERSONE
description: Traversone, also known as Ciapano, Rovescino, Tressette a non Prendere, Perdivinci, or Vinciperdi, is an Italian reverse Tressette trick-taking game. Players follow Tressette play but try to avoid taking point cards; the player who accumulates the penalty total loses unless a successful cappotto reverses the result.

Traversone, also called Ciapano and Rovescino, is the reverse game of Tressette. It is a Lombardy and central Italian trick-taking game whose objective is to avoid taking point cards.
40-card Italian deck. Rank high to low follows Tressette: 3, 2, Ace, King, Knight, Jack, 7, 6, 5, 4.
Deal all possible cards equally, anticlockwise; with four players each receives 10 cards.

items.text: Busca: Four-player variant in which players must take at least one point but avoid taking the most points; the Ace of Coins is a special high-value card.
Mattazza: Four-player variant in which both the highest and lowest point totals can be punished, making the middle score safest.
